beats.text: In Part 7, every step was one of two kinds of tool: plain **code**, or a language **model**.
There is a third kind in between. A small **typed** model reads text, and answers a typed question with a **probability**.
Code is exact. One rule check took about **forty** nanoseconds, and costs nothing.
The typed model answered in about **twenty** milliseconds on the GPU, and about **five hundred** on a plain CPU, with no tokens at all.
The language model is the only one that can **write**. One note took about **two and a half** seconds, and over two hundred tokens.
In the end, the question is not which tool is best. It is which tool this **step** needs.
